original_question: Do there exist wandering domains for complex Henon maps?
target_in_paper: The draft is aiming at the long-standing open problem in the dynamics part of The Several Complex Variables Problem List concerning whether a complex polynomial Hénon map can have a wandering Fatou component; in later official formulations of the same problem this is sharpened to the dissipative case.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the central dynamical phenomenon (wandering domains) and the intended family of maps (complex Hénon maps). It is very close to the standard informal wording used in the Hénon-map literature.
missing_details: In this literature, 'wandering domain' should be stated as 'wandering Fatou component', or equivalently a Fatou component that is not preperiodic.
The ambient space should be specified: the maps act on C^2.
The paper-faithful Hénon setting is polynomial, not arbitrary holomorphic automorphisms and not later transcendental Hénon maps.
A generalized complex Hénon map should be identified explicitly, e.g. f(x,y)=(y,p(y)-δx) with p in C[y], deg p at least 2, and δ in C*.
Later official formulations isolate the dissipative regime |δ|<1; your draft omits this restriction.
The existential quantifier should range over both the map and the Fatou component: does there exist such a map having at least one wandering Fatou component?
If one wants to stay maximally faithful to the polynomial-automorphism literature, one should avoid broadening from a single generalized Hénon map to arbitrary polynomial maps of C^2.
The question should not be broadened to transcendental Hénon maps, since later work constructs wandering domains there and treats that as a different setting.
refined_question: Does there exist a dissipative complex polynomial Hénon map f:C^2→C^2 of the form f(x,y)=(y,p(y)-δx), where p∈C[y] has degree at least 2 and 0<|δ|<1, that has a wandering Fatou component; that is, a Fatou component Ω whose forward images f^n(Ω) are pairwise distinct for all n≥0?
justification: The 1995 arXiv item is a problem list rather than a theorem paper, and its full body text was not retrievable through the browser. To pin down the intended mathematical scope, I used later primary expositions by experts on complex Hénon dynamics. Bedford’s notes give the clean official formulation 'Can a dissipative Hénon map have a wandering Fatou component?' and define a generalized complex Hénon map as a polynomial diffeomorphism of C^2 of the form f(x,y)=(y,p(y)-δx). Arosio–Benini–Fornæss–Peters then confirm that the unresolved problem for polynomial Hénon maps is exactly the existence of wandering domains, while distinguishing this from the transcendental Hénon setting and defining the relevant types of wandering domains. This makes your draft essentially correct in intent, but incomplete because it omits the ambient space C^2, the polynomial/generalized-Hénon form, the Fatou-component formulation, and the dissipative restriction that later official formulations use.
